how_customers_find_and_choose: Patients search the map listing for the nearest trusted provider and read reviews about waiting time and how they were treated
Referral from a doctor, a relative or a friend still matters most, especially for serious or sensitive care
Patients message to ask about timings, availability of a doctor and how to book before they come
Clear information on who the doctors are, what services exist and how to reach the clinic builds trust
Families choose elder and home care mainly on reputation, staff quality and responsiveness to questions
what_works_now: A complete map listing with hours, doctor names, services and a phone or chat contact
Appointment booking by chat or phone with a reminder the day before to cut missed visits
Clear wait-time and cost information given when booking, and the policy for cancellations
Polite, quick reply to patient messages with a person handling them at set hours
Reminders for follow-up visits, vaccinations, screenings or repeat tests where the clinic keeps patient records
Respectful handling of patient information: only the minimum is shared in chat
Educational posts and messages that explain, in plain words, how the clinic can help, without promises of results
outdated_or_weak: Advertising guaranteed cures, results or comparative claims about other providers
Before and after photos of patients without clear consent
Discount offers on medical treatment as the main selling point
Printed pamphlets as the main source of new patients
Chasing patients with repeated promotional messages

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Patients often pay in cash at the counter; insurance coverage varies by clinic and employer
Seasonal illness patterns and Ramadan fasting affect visit patterns and timings
Health care providers are regulated by the medical and pharmacy authorities; the owner confirms specifics with them
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Insurance is central; patients check which providers are covered before booking
Health care is licensed by the health authority, which also sets rules on advertising and patient data; the owner confirms specifics
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Public health care is the first point; private clinics serve allied care such as dental, physiotherapy and therapy
Health information is protected by privacy rules; the owner confirms specifics with the regulator

never_assume: A website or a booking link
Permission to share patient photos or stories
